requiredPrograms.title: Browser-level Repair and Resume fault injection
Frozen and discarded page lifecycle research and recovery
Long-conversation observation, scanning, rendering, timer, and constrained-device performance
Host-affixed mobile Ghost shell research, implementation, and certification
requiredPrograms.mountingRequirement: Attach Ghost into each site's real row/column layout so the host page reflows around it. Blue and red viewport overlays are prohibited.
requiredPrograms.fallback: Keep the current rail only when an adapter cannot pass structural mount verification.

phases.title: Map structural mount contracts for supported platform adapters
Implement structural mount registry and verification/repair primitives
Implement blue composer cell and red expandable sibling row behind an experimental flag
Implement teal header action cell where adapter structure permits
Mobile, accessibility, keyboard, layout-shift, and lower-end performance certification
Expand and certify structural mount contracts across supported platforms
Devil's Advocate and customer-voice review of the host-affixed shell

requiredPrograms.title: Canonical build, candidate, and release-channel identity
Architecture, README, help, changelog, and protocol reconciliation
Full certification, release audit, package, and SHA-256 verification

assignments.goal: Reproduce and specify a browser-level Repair and Resume fault-injection matrix.
assignments.auditVerdict: Accepted as an implementation contract; it does not claim browser execution.

assignments.goal: Implement the smallest Repair and Resume browser fault-injection fixtures and regression coverage required by Worker 2's contract.
assignments.auditVerdict: Fixture exists, but focused Chromium did not complete and runtime faults use a synthetic model rather than the actual production Repair & Resume services.

assignments.goal: Attempt to falsify Worker 3's Repair and Resume coverage using races, repeated subtree replacement, route changes, stale state, uncertain Send, and rapid pause/resume sequences.
assignments.auditVerdict: CI cancellation was correctly diagnosed, but repeated replacement, rapid pause/resume, stale-work resurrection, and production-path fault injection were not executed.

assignments.goal: Evaluate the round's Repair and Resume path under mobile Chromium viewport/lifecycle pressure and measure whether recovery polling, observers, timers, or repeated scans remain bounded.
assignments.rationale: A browser fault fix that is correct on desktop can still regress Android and lower-end devices.
acceptanceCriteria: Run or define a mobile Chromium fault scenario
Record timer/observer/scan counts or bounded proxies
Check viewport resize and background/foreground transitions where harness permits
Confirm no accessibility-visible duplicate status/control is introduced
requiredTests: Playwright mobile Chromium project or equivalent emulation
assignments.fallbackWork: If mobile browser execution is unavailable, add deterministic instrumentation assertions and document the exact CI/browser command needed.
assignments.auditVerdict: Useful mobile fixture scaffolding, but unexecuted and based on synthetic counters rather than production resource or real-device measurements.

assignments.goal: Audit every round-1 assignment, commit, diff, test claim, CI run, generated parity result, and evidence file; accept, reject, or require more evidence for each assignment and close the round for human verification.

roundDecision.summary: Round 1 produced an accepted Repair & Resume fault contract and useful browser/mobile fixture scaffolding, but production-path execution, exact-head Chromium/mobile CI, adversarial replacement/race evidence, and real-device performance remain unresolved.
